Subject Proposed demonstration by the All Shanghai Association for

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford i. s.

The All Shanghai Association for the Support of Armed
Resistance, of which Mr. Dao Pah-chuen (陶百川 ), committee
member of local Tangpu, is one of the leading members, issued
on the night of October 9/10 urgent instructions to all
members of local public bodies ordering them to assemble at
the corner of Nanking and Chekiang Roads at 11 a.m., October 10
for the purpose of conducting a "Peaceful demonstration and
oath-taking ceremony." It is expected that the gathering
will shout the three slogans which are to be broadcasted
by the local Tangpu at 12 noon, and also sing the Chinese
national anthem.
It is expected that should the weather improve, more
than one thousand persons will participate in this movement.

In commemoration of the anniversary of the Double Tenth
Festival, the National Day of China, which falls on October
10, the following services sponsored by various local
Chinese bodies will be observed in the International
Settlement and French Concession :-
- Meetings
In compliance with an order from the local Tangpu,
public bodies and schools will hold a celebration service
in their respective offices or buildings at 10 a.m.
October 10.

Shanghai Association for the Support of Armed Resistance

Support Resistance against the Enemy) (上海各界抗敵後援會)

Subject Tiffin Party held in the Dah Si Yang Restaurant on occasion

Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

Between 12.30 p.m. and 1 p.m., October 10th, Mr. Dao
Pah-chuen was interviewed by C.D.I. Sharman, D.I. Crawford
and D.I. Pan Lien-pih at the Dah Si Yang Restaurant, 710
Foochow Road, where it was explained to him the embarrassment
he was causing the Settlement authorities through demonstrations
and poster distribution and the injudicious way he was using
the Settlement for means of propaganda. It was impressed
upon him that such might lead to incidents and mob violence
and destroy the world wide sympathy China had gained recently
in addition to making it very hard for the Municipal Police
to maintain order in a place where thousands were seeking
refuge. Mr. Dao Pah-chuen replied that he would do everything
possible in an endeavour to persuade those responsible for
the demonstration and poster distribution to desist, but
he was not responsible for that part of the programme, only
the slogans to be broadcasted and an appeal to the people
through the press to be patriotic.

C. Garrod

LOCAL TANGPU DIRECTS CELEBRATION OF OCTOBER 10TH

In view of the approach of the National Day
(October 10) which falls this year at a time when a major war
of resistance against Japan on all fronts is going on, as
well as the fact that the celebration of the same must be
adapted to our needs during this period of emergency so as
to strengthen the war of resistance, the following measures
governing celebration of the anniversary have been drawn up
by the local Tangpu :-
"To celebrate the National Day, all official
organs, public bodies, factories, shops and residences shall
be directed in a circular notice in the newspapers to hoist
the National Flag, and competent officials of organs, public
bodies, schools and factories in question shall lead their
subordinates in holding celebration ceremonies at their
respective places at 10 a.m. October 10. The ceremony must
be held in a simple manner. Besides giving reports or
speeches, the chairman of the ceremony shall direct his
subordinates to subscribe to the Liberty Bonds or the comfort
funds."
The local Tangpu will appoint officials to
broadcast ceremonial procedure through radio stations at
10 a.m. October 10.

In connection with the celebration of the
approaching Double Tenth Festival, the Cultural Circles'
National Extinction Aversion Association yesterday agreed
upon the following measures :-
1) That publicity cards bearing the picture of the late
Dr. Sun Yat-sen be printed.
2) That papers containing caricatures be published.

notified to post up pairs of scrolls inscribed with
characters celebrating the Festival.

through radio stations.

Tenth Festival occasion.
7) That local citizens introduce a "one-cent contribution
movement" on the National Day.
8) That various public bodies hold their respective
celebration ceremonies.
9) That the Entertainers' National Extinction Aversion
Association be arranged to proceed with soliciting
through radio broadcasting stations funds in aid of
refugee camps and hospitals for wounded soldiers.

provide posters to be pasted on walls in their own
alleyways or those in the vicinity; that they be also
notified to distribute publicity matters and to hold
touring choral performances.

CELEBRATION OF THE DOUBLE TENTH ANNIVERSARY

In view of the fact that the National
Anniversary Day, the Double Tenth Festival, this year falls
at a time when China is waging an unanimous war of resistance
against Japan and considering that the celebration of the
anniversary this time should be adapted to the present
circumstances and requirements so as to intensify the
strength of our resistance, the Propaganda Committee of the
Enemy-Resisting Support Association has proposed to urge
the people throughout the country to carry out the enforcement
of the following three movements, namely:-
(1) The movement to subscribe articles for the
comfort of officers and men at the front.
(2) The movement to subscribe contributions
towards the Liberty Bonds.
(3) The movement to call for the severance
of economic relations with Japan.
Certain members have already been appointed
by the Presidium of the Association to form respective
committees to look after the promotion of these movements.

SHANGHAI TIMES - 6.10.37.

Three Movements Launched
To Commemorate October 10

National Independence Day Of China Will Be
Marked This Year By Providing Troops With
Comforts And Selling Liberty Bonds

To commemorate the National Independence Day on October 10, in a manner compatible with the present defensive war against Japan, three important movements will be launched here by the All-Shanghai Association for the Support of Armed Resistance on that day.

The three campaigns are intended to "comfort" Chinese defenders now operating on the Shanghai front, to promote the sale of the Liberty Bonds and to propose the severance of economic, social and cultural relations with Japan.

In the "comfort" movement, the association hopes to gather 100,000 cotton-pad waistcoats and 100,000 "comfort" bags on October 10 to be distributed to the Chinese defenders here.

In this connection, it is learned that Mr. Tu Yueh-sheng, well-known local banker and chairman of the Shanghai Civic Association, has already alone contributed 30,000 cotton waistcoats and 4,000 suits of underwear.

In addition to these "comfort" articles, souvenir banners will be presented to every division or brigade fighting here as an encouragement.

Liberty Bonds

Regarding the promotion of the sale of the Liberty Bonds, the All-Shanghai Association for the Support of Armed Resistance will divide the city into different sections in which a solicitation movement will be launched. Every shop, school and terrace in each locality will be asked to pledge a certain amount of the bonds. To bring this movement to a success, solicitation parties will be organised for activities in these sections.

A boycott on Japanese goods to echo the world-wide clamouring to this effect will start the movement for severing all relations with Japan.

On October 10, a well-organized and determined boycott movement will be launched here and a supervisory committee will be organized to supervise and encourage its Central News.

以纪念十月十日

CELEBRATION OF THE CHINESE NATIONAL DAY: MEASURES DRAWN UP
BY TANGPU

The following measures for the celebration of the
Chinese National Day, which falls on October 10, have been
published by the local Tangpu Headquarters:-
(1) All official organs, public organizations, schools,
factories, shops and residents will fly the National Flag
to celebrate the day.
(2) The persons in charge of official organs, public organiza-
tions and schools will lead their subordinates to hold
commemoration meetings at their respective places at
10 a.m. October 10, and to purchase Liberty Bonds,
subscribe to the Comfort Fund or contribute relief
articles such as cotton-padded jackets, waistcoats, quilts,
etc. The citizens in general should also make contribu-
tions voluntarily.
(3) An official of the Tangpu will lead the people, through
the radio, in shouting the following slogans at noon
October 10:-
Long Live the Three Principles of the People!
Long Live the Chinese Kuomintang!
Long Live the Republic of China!

Notice of Chamber of Commerce

The Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce has issued a notice instructing all factories and shops to hoist the National Flag on October 10 in celebration of the National Day, and owners of motor trucks, hire cars and private cars to fly the National Flag on their vehicles.

Outline of Propaganda Issued by Enemy-Resisting Association

The Propaganda Committee of the Shanghai Various Circle Enemy-Resisting Association yesterday published the following outline of propaganda relating to the National Day.-
(1) The Significance of This Year's National Day.
(a) The unity of the Chinese people has strengthened as a result of the resistance put up by us on all fronts.
(b) To support the Government, trust our leader and sacrifice everything for a lasting war of resistance is the unanimous advocacy of the whole nation.
(c) All the people, without any distinction whatever, should fight for the liberty and equality of China.
(d) We have begun to settle the accounts of humiliation we have suffered in the past.
(e) This year's National Day marks the beginning of a resistance put up by a peaceful force against an aggressive force.
(f) This year's National Day sees all peace-loving and just nations of the world join hands with China to deal a severe blow to the aggressor.
(g) This year's National Day shows a bright future for our resistance against the enemy.
(2) How Shall We Celebrate This Year's National Day?
(a) Sever our economic relations with Japan.
(b) Help to raise the Liberty Loan.
(c) Comfort the officers and men at the front.

Contemplated Activities of Other Organizations

The Shanghai Relief Commission will explain to refugees in the various camps on October 10 the meaning of National Day and national salvation. A general outline of propaganda has been drawn up and instructors of refugees have been ordered to conduct propaganda according to the outline.

The Shanghai Boy Scouts' War-Time Service Corps will distribute National Day cakes and clothing to wounded soldiers and refugees on the National Day.
The Propaganda Section of the Corps will conduct a special radio broadcast on that day.

On the instruction of the Shanghai Enemy-Resisting Support Association, members of the National Extinction Aversion Association of Shanghai Students Who Have Undergone Military Training will conduct propaganda urging people to contribute comforting articles and subscribe to the Liberty Loan. They will gather at and set out from the Mei Hwa (美华) Girls' Middle School, Carter Road, at 8 a.m. October 10.

抗敌协会发布的宣传大纲

上海各界抗敌协会宣传部昨日发布了以下关于国庆的宣传大纲：-
(1) 今年国庆的意义。
(a) 由于我们在各条战线上的抵抗，中国人民的团结得到了加强。
(b) 支持政府，信任我们的领袖，并为持久抗战牺牲一切，是全国一致的主张。
(c) 全体人民，不分彼此，都应为中国的自由和平等而战。
(d) 我们已开始清算过去所受的屈辱。
(e) 今年的国庆标志着和平力量对抗侵略力量的抵抗的开始。
(f) 今年的国庆见证了全世界所有爱好和平与正义的国家与中国携手，给予侵略者沉重打击。
(g) 今年的国庆显示了我们抗敌的光明前景。
(2) 我们应如何庆祝今年的国庆？
(a) 断绝与日本的经济关系。
(b) 协助募集救国公债。
(c) 慰劳前线官兵。

其他组织的计划活动

上海救济委员会将于10月10日向各难民营的难民解释国庆和救国的意义。已制定宣传大纲，并命令难民指导员按照该大纲进行宣传。

上海童子军战时服务团将在国庆日向伤兵和难民分发国庆糕点和衣物。
该团的宣传股将在当天进行特别无线电广播。

根据上海抗敌后援会的指示，上海学生军事训练灭耻会成员将进行宣传活动，敦促人们捐献慰问品并认购救国公债。他们将于10月10日上午8时在卡特路（Carter Road）美华女中集合出发。

Hwa Mei Wan Pao of October 8 :-

GENERAL TSAI TING-KAI TO RETURN TO SHANGHAI

Due to the fact that his wife had died of sickness
in Hongkong, General Tsai Ting-kai, ex-Commander of the
defunct 19th Route Army, left here for Hongkong in September
to cope with funeral arrangements.
It is now learned that, having completed all
necessary affairs, General Tsai has proceeded to Nanking
whence he will come to Shanghai to continue his part in the
anti-Japanese campaign.

--------------------------------------------------
At 8 p.m. on the 9-10-37, F.S.277 Potapoff brought
to the Station the underdescribed male Chinese, who in
company with three or four others who decamped, was seen
preparing to stick certain posters on the walls at the
corner of Kiangse and Canton Roads:

native of Ningpo, employed at the Great China
Dispensary, 313 Foochow Road.
He was found to be in possession of seven posters
each stamped with the seal of the "Shanghai Vocational
Young Men's War Service Society Propaganda Section" and
bearing either one of the following slogans:
"Celebrate the National Day and fight to the end."
"Who caused the separation of your families and the
destruction of your homes"
On interrogation by C.D.S.s 86, and 117 Zee Ts Oen
stated that he had obtained the posters from a certain
address on Kiangse Road, to which he had been invited by
a fellow employee named Lieu Hwei Sung(劉惠松). He
alleged he was not aware of the identity of his four
companions who had decamped at the time of his arrest
and at whose request he was prepared to assist in
distributing the posters.

Report on posters found pasted in Central District bearing slogans
for Chinese People in connection with the "Double Tenth" Incident.
Det. Insp. A. Telfer,

Sir,

During the morning of October 10th 1937 posters were found
pasted up at various places in Central District bearing the
following slogans:-

1. Labourers and capitalists unite together to counter
invasion.

2. Push the sale of native goods and boycott the Japanese
goods.

3. Urge our Government to sever diplomatic relations with
Japan.

4. Increase the rate of production to acquire victory
by defence.

5. To celebrate the "Double Tenth" Anniversary needs
the spirit of our late martyrs.

6. We have celebrated this year's "Double Tenth" with
gunfire.

7. We should carry out the "work of rescuing" with honesty.

8. Plead our Government to give aid to the unemployed.

9. Stick to "Land-burnt" defence.

10. Our young female and male compatriots should unanimously
work for the Nation.

11. Prefer to die for our Fatherland rather than to live
as slaves without a nation.

12. Support our Government to defend to the end.

13. Give bitter punishment to the invaders.

14. Up with the slogan "Not an inch of lost land with the celebration
of the Double Tenth".

15. Contribute old cotton-padded clothing and bedcovers to
the refugees.

16. It is by whose bestowal that we departed with our wives
and offspring!

17. Wake up the whole race.

18. Struggle and defend to the end.

19. Long live the emancipation of the whole race.

At 12.07 p.m. 10/10/37 S.I. Moffat together with S.I.s

were patrolling District in the Station raiding van, on arrival
at Ave. Ed. VII Lungmen Road a party of male and female Chinese
of the student type numbering about 20, were seen to be staging
a demonstration outside Nanking Cinema on north side of Ave. Ed.
VII. They were warned to desist and left in an easterly direc-
tion towards Yu Ya Ching Road, the Police party followed them,
and on arrival at Yu Ya Ching and Ave. Ed. VII intersection,
another party of approx. 200 came from south to north on Rue de
Montigny and congregated around the traffic island at Ave. Ed.
VII Yu Ye Ching Road and proceeded to stage a demonstration
shouting Anti-Japanese slogans and holding up all traffic on
Ave. Ed. VII. They were asked to desist, which they refused to
do and adopted a hostile attitude, and attempted to pass Police
party and proceed north on Yu Ya Ching Road, assistance was then
called for and rendered by three members of the S.V.C. Russian
Unit and four C.P.C.s on post duty at said corner. Police and
S.V.C. then lined themselves across Ave. Ed. VII, demonstrators
on observing this show of strength turned east on French side of
Ave. Ed. VII and marched off shouting slogans. French Police &
Douai Station were immediately informed and attended, escorting
east

VII）龙门路时，看到一群约20人的男女中国学生在爱多亚路北侧的南京大戏院外进行示威。警方警告其停止，他们向东朝虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）方向离开，警察队伍跟随他们，到达虞洽卿路与爱多亚路交叉口时，另一群约200人从南向北沿蒙梯尼路（Rue de Montigny）走来，聚集在爱多亚路与虞洽卿路的交通岛周围，并开始进行示威，高呼抗日口号，阻塞了爱多亚路上的所有交通。警方要求其停止，但他们拒绝并表现出敌对态度，试图穿过警察队伍沿虞洽卿路向北行进，随后呼叫援助，由三名俄国籍上海志愿队（S.V.C.）成员和四名在该角落执勤的中国巡捕（C.P.C.s）提供协助。警察和上海志愿队随即在爱多亚路上排成一列，示威者看到这一武力展示后，转向爱多亚路的法租界一侧向东行进，高呼口号离开。已立即通知法国警察及杜美巡捕房（Douai Station），他们到场并护送

离开。

1.

Two male Chinese arrested for posting anti-Japanese
pamphlets.

At 12-45pm. on 10/10/37 Special Constable 0.962
J. S. Kenishkis brought to this station the underdescribed
two male Chinese whom he had observed posting
pamphlets of an Anti-Japanese nature on Sinza Road
near Myburgh Road.

1. Lee Lung( 李 隆 ) aged 21, native of Wusieh,
M/unemployed, residing No.7 Chungking Road.

2. Tang Zen Kung( 唐 振 公 ) aged 23, native of
Shanghai, S/unemployed, residing No.5 Suh Pien Loong
Road, Nantao.

They were in possession of a number of sheets of
red paper on which Chinese characters were written
with a Chinese pen and ink, urging the people to be
patriotic and resist Japan, also various Anti-Japanese
phrases.

They stated that they are members of the "Youths'
League to resist Agression", and that on 9/10/37 the
head of their League, Chang Hyang Choong( 張 向 忠 ),
told them to attend the fourth floor of the Sinza
Lodging House, No.841 Sinza Road on 10/10/37.

They arrived there at about 9am. on 10/10/37 with
about 20 other members of the League, and were given
the seized pamphlets to post in the Settlement. They
left the Lodging House at 12-30pm. and had posted
several bills before being arrested.

1.

两名中国男子因张贴反日小册子被捕。

1937年10月10日下午12点45分，特别巡警 0.962 号 J. S. Kenishkis 将下述两名中国男子带至本捕房，他此前观察到这两人在靠近麦根路 (Myburgh Road) 的新闸路上张贴具有反日性质的小册子。

1. 李隆 (Lee Lung)，21岁，吴淞 (Wusieh) 人，未婚/失业，居住于重庆路7号。

2. 唐振公 (Tang Zen Kung)，23岁，上海人，单身/失业，居住于南市苏宾弄路 (Suh Pien Loong Road) 5号。

他们持有数张红纸，上面用中国毛笔和墨水书写着汉字，呼吁民众爱国并抵抗日本，以及各种反日口号。

他们声称自己是“青年抗敌联盟”的成员，并称该联盟负责人张向忠 (Chang Hyang Choong) 于1937年10月9日告知他们，于1937年10月10日前往新闸路841号新闸旅社四楼集合。

他们于1937年10月10日上午9点左右到达那里，当时另有约20名联盟成员在场，他们领取了被查获的小册子以便在租界内张贴。他们于中午12点30分离开旅社，在被捕前已张贴了几张告示。

12.Without the Country we cannot gain freedom.

1. Don't buy Japanese goods!
2. Kill the Japanese devils in China!
3. Down with Japanese dwarfs!
4. Cancel all unequal treaties signed between China and Japan!
5. Chase away the Japanese Ambassador in China!
6. Confiscate the Japanese property in China!

报告
日期 1937年10月10日

事由......在虹口西区发现反日宣传品。

由陶庚永（Tao Keng Yong）副巡官撰写。由参谋中尉 J.C. 转呈

先生，
1937年10月10日上午8点，萨德勒（S.S. Sadler）高级警员和克兰（P.S. Crane）警佐将一幅鼓励国民购买救国公债并奋起抗日的漫画带至捕房，该漫画张贴于北浙江路；此外还有今早在虹口西区各条道路墙壁上发现的以下海报。
1. 不买日货！
2. 杀死在华的日本鬼子！
3. 打倒日本矮子！
4. 废除中日之间签订的所有不平等条约！
5. 驱逐在华日本大使！
6. 没收在华日本财产！
7. 不允许任何日本人进入中国！
8. 与日本断绝关系！
9. 消除日本军国主义！
10. 清除汉奸！与日本断绝经济关系！！！

陶庚永
副巡官（D. S. I.）

主管高级侦探（Sen. Det. 1/c.）。

“G”区副警务处长（D.D.O.）。

罗斯（Ross），
刑事侦缉处特别支部。
